title: Restoration After Failure
definition: Restoration after failure is God's gracious work of bringing repentant people back into renewed obedience, fellowship, usefulness, and hope.
summary: Failure does not have to be the final word when there is repentance and grace.
christFocus: Jesus restores fallen people through mercy and truth, as seen in His restoration of Peter.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Failure is painful, but Scripture shows that God restores repentant sinners. Restoration does not deny sin or remove all consequences, but it brings hope where shame says everything is over.

David's prayer in Psalm 51 and Peter's restoration by Jesus show that God can renew broken servants. Repentance, confession, humility, accountability, and grace are part of the path.

Restoration is not a return to pride or carelessness. It is renewed dependence on God and renewed faithfulness after mercy has been received.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people believe failure permanently disqualifies them from God's care or usefulness. Restoration after failure matters because it proclaims that Christ is able to forgive, heal, and recommission repentant people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess failure honestly and seek wise help. Receive Christ's mercy, accept necessary correction, and take humble steps of renewed obedience rather than living under permanent shame.
